correctness.rationale: For the integer digit gap (as required by the digit and gcd setup), grouping by the top frequency bit and last spatial bit removes the cross term with the previous spatial prefix modulo one. The only remaining twist is diagonal unitary on the lower frequencies. The product factorization is singular exactly when a level has dt divisible by b. Upon inverting, the two blocks of a selected inverse row are scalar multiples of the same lower-level row, with a unitary right twist. Its norm squared therefore multiplies by 1/(2ps²) or 1/(2(1-p)s²), as given by the two-by-two inverse. The inverse Gram diagonal equals that row norm squared. Summing the inverse masses yields the trace; the block determinants yield the stated modulus with exponent N/2 per level. The trace is minimized exactly by maximizing every sine and every p(1-p); for the largest diagonal the minimum cell mass is at most 1/N with equality only for uniform masses. All nonzero residues modulo q are attained, enough for the stated congruences; the proof's claim about all residue classes need not include zero when gcd(b,d)=1. At the even-q optimum each level block is unitary, and at odd q the mean of reciprocal squared singular values and the row normalization give the obstructions without claiming equality. Independent construction from integer residues and direct Gram solves checked 180 positive-weight nonsingular cases (max relative diagonal error 6.69e-14), 210 cases with exactly one zero-sine level, and unitary and nonunitary optima through depth 5. The all-depth proof is exact, not numerical.
residual_risks: Scope is a square finite integer-digit tower with positive Bernoulli product masses. The quoted obstructions for singular matrices mean zero least singular value and infinite condition number; inverse objectives are defined on nonsingular choices.
Editorially state 'integer digit gap' and 'all nonzero residues' explicitly; neither wording point affects the substantive inference on the stated digit setup.

value.rationale: The coordinatewise noise-amplification law addresses the inverse problem for a natural tower, not just the volume of its sampling map. It shows exactly how smaller masses increase local estimation variance, makes the A and worst-coordinate objectives share all optimizers with explicit parity costs, and improves an instability obstruction. These provide usable design and inverse-conditioning information not determined by a known determinant alone.
residual_risks: Does not establish optimal arbitrary-frequency designs, exact singular-value extrema, or an infinite-measure theorem.
